title: FBI Proffer Recorded a Witness’s Claim That Epstein Introduced Melania to Trump
description_short: A redacted former Epstein assistant told the FBI that Epstein introduced Melania and Donald Trump; the claim remains disputed.
description_medium: An FBI proffer record from 2019 was reported to contain a redacted former assistant’s statement that Jeffrey Epstein introduced Melania Trump to Donald Trump. The report says the interview occurred in July 2019 and that the document is dated November 2019. The statement is an allegation, not an established account of how the couple met; public accounts described different introductions. The record does not substantiate the original 209-file count.
description_long: In a 2019 FBI proffer, a redacted former assistant to Jeffrey Epstein said that Epstein introduced Melania Trump to Donald Trump. The Daily Beast reported that the witness made the claim during a July 2019 interview with FBI agents and federal prosecutors, and quoted the heavily redacted record as stating that Epstein introduced Melania to Donald Trump. The underlying allegation remains unverified. The article noted that the claim conflicts with Melania Trump’s memoir and with Donald Trump’s account, and reported that the Justice Department had warned that the file release could contain false or falsely submitted material. The FBI record’s November 2019 date refers to the document, while the interview was in July 2019; neither supports the frozen entry’s 2002 date. This draft therefore centers the reported contents of one proffer and omits the claim that Melania appears in 209 EFTA documents, because the supplied record cites no verifiable count for that number. It does not infer knowledge, participation, or wrongdoing from a witness statement.

source_fact_map.fact: The report says the witness made the claim in July 2019.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: The unnamed woman, a former model who worked as Epstein’s assistant for a year from 2005 to 2006, made the claim in July 2019, three days after her old boss was arrested by the FBI and charged with child sex trafficking. The 11-page, heavily redacted document was published in Friday’s dump of three million Epstein files and uncovered on Monday. The woman’s claim contradicts Melania Trump’s memoir’s version of her meet-cute with her billionaire husband, as well as what he has said about how they became a couple. The White House pointed to a previous warning from the Department of Justice that the Epstein files may contain untrue information. The bombshell claim about the couple’s origin story appeared in an FBI record dated November 2019, which details a July interview with a woman whose name was redacted—and who was given immunity to speak. The interview was with both FBI agents and career federal prosecutors, and is recorded as a “proffer agreement.” Several lines of text were redacted before continuing: “ZEMPOLI was trying to buy Elite Models with EPSTEIN. EPSTEIN introduced MELANIA TRUMP to DONALD TRUMP.”

title: Trump Said He Knew More About Courts Than Anyone in November 2015
description_short: Trump said, “I know more about courts than any human being on Earth,” at a Texas rally in November 2015.
description_medium: A January 2019 Axios review of Trump’s claims of expertise quotes him saying, “I know more about courts than any human being on Earth,” and dates the statement to November 2015. The frozen entry’s 2019 date aligns with the later article’s publication year, not the reported statement. Axios identifies a Texas rally but does not provide a specific day or city.
description_long: At a Texas rally in November 2015, Donald Trump said, “I know more about courts than any human being on Earth,” according to a January 2019 Axios review that cited The Washington Post’s reporting for the date. This entry records the boast itself. It does not treat the statement as evidence of legal expertise, a factual assessment of court performance, or proof of any particular legal outcome. The frozen entry dated the quote to 2019 and surrounded it with claims about Trump’s litigation history, legal misjudgments, expert criticism, and the 2020 election; those assertions are outside the cited passage and are not retained here. The reporting supports a month and year, but not the precise day of the rally or its city, so the date uses month-level precision. This correction separates the date of the statement from the date of the 2019 article that catalogued it. No additional event or later legal dispute is substituted for the original quote.

title: Bondi DOJ Working Group Ordered Review of Federal Actions Involving Alvin Bragg
description_short: A February 2025 DOJ memo directed a working-group review that included alleged federal cooperation with Alvin Bragg’s Trump prosecution.
description_medium: On February 5, 2025, Attorney General Pam Bondi created the DOJ Weaponization Working Group and directed it to review federal enforcement activity from the previous four years. The memo included alleged federal cooperation with Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s Trump prosecution among the subjects for review. It did not establish that allegation, announce a Bragg-specific criminal investigation, or find that Bragg acted improperly.
description_long: On February 5, 2025, Attorney General Pam Bondi issued a memo establishing the Justice Department’s Weaponization Working Group. The directive assigned the group a review of federal civil and criminal enforcement activities during the previous four years and called for quarterly progress reports to the White House. Its list of topics included what the memo called “federal cooperation with the weaponization” by Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg, New York Attorney General Letitia James, their staffs, and other New York officials against Donald Trump and his businesses. That language states the administration’s allegation and the subject of a review; it is not a finding that Bragg coordinated with federal authorities or acted unlawfully. The memo also does not announce a criminal investigation into Bragg. The frozen entry’s claim that DOJ opened a February investigation into Bragg, along with its assertions about Bragg’s cooperation and a coordinated campaign against prosecutors, is not supported by the material reviewed and is omitted. The documented event is the DOJ review directive concerning the earlier Trump prosecutions.

source_fact_map.fact: Bondi’s February 5 memo established a DOJ Weaponization Working Group.
source_fact_map.quote: February 5, 2025 MEMORANDUM FOR ALL DEPARTMENT EMPLOYEES
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: February 5, 2025 MEMORANDUM FOR ALL DEPARTMENT EMPLOYEES FROM: THE ATTORNEY GENERAL SUBJECT: RESTORING THE INTEGRITY AND CREDIBILITY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE. I hereby establish the Weaponization Working Group, which will be led by the Office of the Attorney General and supported by the Office of the Deputy Attorney General, the Office of Legal Policy, the Civil Rights Division, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia, and other personnel as necessary to achieve the objectives set forth herein. The Weaponization Working Group will conduct a review of the activities of all departments and agencies exercising civil or criminal enforcement authority of the United States over the last four years, in consultation with the heads of such departments and agencies and consistent with applicable law, to identify instances where a department’s or agency’s conduct appears to have been designed to achieve political objectives or other improper aims rather than pursuing justice or legitimate governmental objectives. The Department of Justice will provide quarterly reports to the White House regarding the progress of the review. During this review, the Weaponization Working Group will examine, among other things: Federal cooperation with the weaponization by the Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg, New York Attorney General Letitia James, their respective staffs, and other New York officials to target President Trump, his family, and his businesses.
